claims.statement: Tom Allen made an unsatisfactory appearance as a boxer in the art gallery of Madison Square Garden on Monday evening, November 27, 1882.
A boxing exhibition complimentary to Tom Allen was given at Madison Square Garden, New York, on Monday evening, November 27.
Tom Allen and George Rooke appeared on stage to round up the exhibition.
At the end of the last round of the exhibition with George Rooke, Tom Allen fell heavily to the floor.
Tom Allen gave an exhibition on Monday, 1882-11-27, which satisfied his backer R. K. Fox that the veteran had seen his best days.
Tom Allen was announced to make his first public appearance in America since returning from England at an exhibition in the Art Gallery of Madison Square Garden, New York.
Tom Allen and George Rooke were set to wind up the exhibition with a bout that was a tame affair, and the audience hissed after the first round.
Tom Allen had a set-to with George Rooke that was agreed to have no rough work.
Tom Allen said he fell in his set-to with George Rooke only because his foot broke through the staging.
Tom Allen was to spar Morris O'Connell in full ring costume at O'Connell's farewell benefit at Tom Kelly's, his first appearance with the gloves since returning to St. Louis.
Tom Allen and Morris O'Connell faced each other in the ring at Kelly's during O'Connell's farewell benefit.
Tom Allen and Morris O'Connell sparred three rounds, which ended the evening's programme.
